resource.name: Food Inspections-Chicago
resource.description: This information is derived from inspections of restaurants and other food establishments in Chicago from January 1, 2010 to the present. Inspections are performed by staff from the Chicago Department of Public Health’s Food Protection Program using a standardized procedure. The results of the inspection are inputted into a database, then reviewed and approved by a State of Illinois Licensed Environmental Health Practitioner (LEHP). For descriptions of the data elements included in this set, please click here. Note about 7/1/2018 change to food inspection procedures that affects the data in this dataset: http://bit.ly/2yWd2JB Disclaimer: Attempts have been made to minimize any and all duplicate inspection reports. However, the dataset may still contain such duplicates and the appropriate precautions should be exercised when viewing or analyzing these data. The result of the inspections (pass, pass with conditions or fail) as well as the violations noted are based on the findings identified and reported by the inspector at the time of the inspection, and may not reflect the findings noted at other times. For more information about Food Inspections, go to https://www.chicago.gov/city/en/depts/cdph/provdrs/food_safety.html.
columns_description: The date of the inspection, which may influence the risk level due to seasonal factors or recent events.
The type of food establishment (e.g., restaurant, grocery store, food truck) which can impact risk levels.
The result of the last inspection prior to the current one, indicating trends in compliance.
The total number of violations noted in the current inspection, which directly relates to risk.
The average rating of the establishment based on past inspections, which can indicate overall compliance.
The neighborhood where the establishment is located, which may have varying health codes and enforcement levels.
How often the establishment is inspected, which can correlate with risk levels.
Indicates whether staff have received food safety training, which can affect compliance and risk.
The density of food establishments in the area, which may influence competition and compliance.
The time of day when the inspection took place, which may affect food safety practices.
Number of recent complaints filed against the establishment, which may indicate potential risk.
